blockers.title: No timeout/AbortSignal on the embedding HTTP call
blockers.finding: safeEmbed catches thrown errors but a hanging (connection-accepted, never-responding) endpoint would block runDomainStage recall, generateDomainProposal recall, and recordHumanDecision writes indefinitely. This matches the pre-existing fetch-without-timeout pattern used by the LLM path (withBackoff retries but has no deadline), and the dominant down-endpoint failure mode (connection refused) fails fast and degrades correctly, so this is a hardening item, not a merge blocker.
evidence: packages/business/src/domain-ai/domain-embedding.ts:25-34 - safeEmbed catches exceptions only; no deadline enforcement
packages/business/src/mail/ai-classify-batch.ts:13-62 - withBackoff has retries but no timeout (pre-existing pattern)
blockers.fixDirection: Wrap the embedding fetch in AbortSignal.timeout(...) or pass a deadline through ResolveEmbedderOptions.

blockers.title: Failed update keeps the stale prior embedding instead of clearing it
blockers.finding: When safeEmbed fails on an UPDATE of an existing row, upsertDomainMemory omits the embedding field so the row keeps its previous (now potentially content-stale) embedding. This is defensible best-effort semantics (do not destroy a known-good vector) but it is undocumented and the dim-guard does not cover same-embedder staleness.
evidence: packages/business/src/domain-ai/domain-memory.ts:171 - ...(input.embedding ? { embedding: input.embedding } : {}) means omitted-on-failure = keep-old-value on the update branch
packages/business/src/domain-ai/domain-agent-runtime.ts:210 and project-decision.ts:89 - callers rely on this omission behavior
blockers.fixDirection: Document the keep-old-vector semantics on upsertDomainMemory, or explicitly decide whether a failed update should null the embedding.
